description: Binding incident-management policy for Memory OS. It defines severity, command roles, containment boundaries, evidence preservation, recovery verification and closure criteria without claiming that paging, external contacts or production drills are configured.
principles: protect user data and tenant isolation before availability or cosmetic recovery
stop destructive or ambiguous automation before attempting cleanup
preserve evidence without copying secrets or personal content into incident notes
distinguish confirmed fact, known prior condition, hypothesis and opinion
do not describe a component retry, transaction rollback or process restart as full recovery
recovery is complete only after independent integrity and non-resurrection verification
unknown state remains quarantined or read-only until classified
incident command owns tradeoffs; individual operators do not improvise destructive recovery

severityLevels.name: CRITICAL_SECURITY_OR_INTEGRITY
examples: confirmed or credible cross-tenant data visibility
destructive memory mutation or deletion resurrection
evidence that production data cannot be trusted

severityLevels.name: MAJOR_AVAILABILITY_OR_DATA_RISK
examples: widespread Import API, PostgreSQL or object-store outage
migration or backfill failure with possible data-integrity impact
unbounded queue, resource exhaustion or repeated internal failures
account deletion or export unavailable for a material user segment

severityLevels.name: DEGRADED_OR_LIMITED_SCOPE
examples: partial feature degradation with bounded impact
elevated latency or retries below a confirmed integrity boundary
single dependency path degraded with safe fallback or fail-closed behavior
operational backlog growing but within a reviewed safety envelope

severityLevels.name: MINOR_OR_INTERNAL_ONLY
examples: documentation, dashboard or test-only issue without production impact
isolated transient failure with no integrity or security concern

responsibilities: declare severity and incident scope
assign roles and approve containment or recovery transitions
maintain a single decision log
escalate when integrity, security or recovery assumptions are uncertain
approve closure only after verification criteria are met
execute approved containment and recovery actions
record exact commands, source SHA and target environment without secrets
report observed outcomes and stop on unclassified state
assess data exposure, unauthorized authority and evidence-preservation needs
own credential rotation and access-restriction decisions
engage legal or privacy review when required by the confirmed facts
explain expected system invariants and dependency boundaries
define integrity verification and safe rollback or forward-fix options
own follow-up remediation acceptance
prepare fact-only internal and user-facing updates
avoid unsupported root-cause, scope or recovery claims
record update timestamps and next review point
maintain the append-only timeline, decisions, evidence references and open hypotheses
separate fact, prior-known condition, inference and opinion
exclude secrets, raw tokens and unnecessary personal content

requiredActions: create incident id and append-only record
record detection source and first confirmed symptom
assign provisional severity and owner
freeze destructive automation for credible integrity or security events
lifecycle.exitCriteria: incident owner, provisional severity and immediate safety posture are explicit

requiredActions: identify affected surfaces, tenants, time window and dependency state
separate confirmed facts from hypotheses
check whether confidentiality, integrity, availability, deletion or authentication invariants are affected
identify evidence that must be preserved before mutation
lifecycle.exitCriteria: current impact and uncertainty are documented well enough to choose containment

requiredActions: prefer fail-closed or read-only behavior when authority or integrity is uncertain
stop affected writes, workers, migrations or credentials only through approved bounded actions
preserve ambiguous object, spool and database state
verify containment did not widen impact or bypass RLS
lifecycle.exitCriteria: active impact is stopped or bounded and containment side effects are understood

requiredActions: capture exact commit, deployment, migration and dependency identifiers
record privacy-safe logs, metrics and database/object metadata references
protect evidence from modification
test hypotheses against independent evidence
lifecycle.exitCriteria: a supported cause or bounded recovery hypothesis exists without destroying evidence

requiredActions: choose application rollback, forward-fix, replay, restore or compensating action explicitly
apply the smallest reversible recovery step
keep destructive cleanup separate from service restoration
record all external side effects that database rollback cannot reverse
lifecycle.exitCriteria: service is restored to a defined state and all recovery mutations are recorded

requiredActions: verify tenant isolation, authentication authority and RLS
verify Preview and Apply accounting and idempotency
verify deletion and expired-session non-resurrection
verify object-version and checksum bindings
verify error rate, latency, backlog and resource trends
run an independent negative test for the initiating failure
lifecycle.exitCriteria: availability and data/security invariants pass independent verification

requiredActions: record final severity, impact and supported root cause
record what remains unknown
assign remediation owners and dates
preserve the timeline and evidence index
schedule or complete a blameless review for SEV0 and SEV1
lifecycle.exitCriteria: required approvals exist and no unresolved critical safety condition remains

mandatoryStopConditions: target environment or database identity is ambiguous
a recovery step requires an unreviewed destructive mutation
cross-tenant visibility or authentication authority is uncertain
the proposed action would delete or overwrite incident evidence
the operator cannot state the exact source commit or deployed version
a restore or rollback would violate deletion or expired-session semantics
required incident command or security/privacy role is unassigned
a command would expose a secret or unrestricted personal content in the incident record

communicationRules.note: No pager, status-page, legal/privacy contact tree or user-notification channel is configured by this contract. Those remain deployment work.

requiredDrillScenarios.scenario: cross-tenant Preview visibility or forged authority
PostgreSQL unavailable during Preview or Apply
restore causes deleted data or expired session to reappear
parser resource escape or untrusted payload compromise

readiness.note: Policy, roles and runbook foundations are defined. Paging, contact ownership, completed tabletop evidence, production-shaped recovery drills and independent review remain missing, so OPS-P0-002 stays PARTIAL.
